course.title: Electronic, Magnetic and Optical Properties of Materials
course.department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering

content.value: Because of a shortage of Cu during World War II, the electromagnets used in Oak Ridge to separate U-235 isotopes for the Hiroshima atomic bomb were wound with pure silver, which has an atomic volume of 10.30 cc/mol. If 100 m of silver wire 2 mm in diameter required 8.1 watts electrical power when carrying 4 amps of current, calculate the (i) resistivity; (ii) electron mobility; (iii) collision time; (iv) mean free path; (v) Hall coefficient and (vi) Hall field in a transverse magnetic field of 9 tesla. You may remember that electrical power equals the product of current & voltage. Assume $\mathrm { T } = 3 0 0 \mathrm { K }$ , silver is monovalent (one free electron per atom) and any other missing data.

_source_title: B.Sc. Engineering 4th Year 1st Term Regular Examination, 2021
